title: Engineering 2D Multifunctional Ultrathin Bismuthene for Multiple Photonic Nanomedicine

nodes.label: Cancer nanomedicine needs one agent that heats, generates ROS and gives imaging contrast under NIR light
2D bismuthene had never been made with the structure and yield biomedicine needs
Water-mediated freeze-thaw exfoliation plus NaBH4 reduction should give few-layered bismuthene with NIR absorbance for photonic therapy
Bulk Bi crystal as feedstock: puckered layered pnictogen, heavy element, cheap and biocompatible

attrs.reason: layered structure allows intercalation; high Z for CT; low cost

nodes.label: Organic-solvent-free route: repeated freezing-thawing with sonication, then NaBH4 reduction

attrs.reason: mass production, low cost, no organic solvent

nodes.label: Coat the sheets with bovine serum albumin to give BNs-BSA for intravenous use
Sweep bismuthene concentration 25-200 ug/mL, 808 nm power 0.5-1.5 W/cm2, and six in-vivo treatment groups

attrs.variable: concentration; laser power density; treatment arm

nodes.label: Five freezing-thawing cycles with ultrasonication expand and delaminate the Bi bulk crystal
NaBH4 reduction of the exfoliated bismuthene oxide nanosheets
Surface functionalisation of the sheets with BSA
Water intercalates the puckered interlayer gap and, on freezing, expands and prises the Bi layers apart
Free-standing ultrathin 2D bismuthene nanosheets, ~200 nm lateral size
Reduced sheets are crystalline rhombohedral Bi (PDF#05-0519); the exfoliated precursor is a Bi-oxide phase (PDF#45-1344)
Direct band gap 0.69 eV with broad vis-NIR absorbance; extinction coefficient 6.4 L/g/cm at 808 nm
Narrow-gap ultrathin semiconductor: 808 nm photons relax non-radiatively to heat, 660 nm photons separate e-h pairs that make singlet oxygen
Photothermal conversion: dispersion heats 31.5 to 57.7 C in 6 min at 200 ug/mL, 1.5 W/cm2; efficiency 19.4%
Bismuthene generates ROS under 660 nm light, bleaching the DPBF probe far faster than water
BNs-BSA gives concentration-linear photoacoustic contrast and raises tumour CT contrast in vivo
Combined 660 + 808 nm irradiation of BNs-BSA eradicates 4T1 tumours with 100% morbidity-free survival

attrs.condition: 100 mW/cm2 at 660 nm and 1 W/cm2 at 808 nm, 6 min

nodes.label: A solvent-free freeze-thaw plus reduction route delivers 2D bismuthene that images and treats tumours by PTT and PDT together
Reduction is partial: Bi(0) grows strongly but Bi2O3 4f components still dominate the bismuthene surface
Bulk Bi has a puckered layered structure with 3.979 A interlayer distance
Graphene oxide, a standard photothermal agent, has an extinction coefficient of 3.6 L/g/cm at 808 nm
Bismuthene absorbs ~1.8x more strongly at 808 nm than graphene oxide
660 nm and 808 nm laser irradiation of dispersions and of tumour-bearing mice

notes: Lost: the supplementary exfoliation series (Figures S1-S3), the in-vitro cell work, biodistribution and biodegradation, and the histology panel F5i. Packet figure ids are offset from the paper: packet F4 carries the paper's Figure 5 caption and packet F5 the paper's Figure 6; the paper's Figure 4 is absent from the record. Two audits: the 14 nm AFM height (o2) undercuts 'few-layered', and the XPS (o5) shows the reduction is only partial. The DPBF probe wavelength is quoted three different ways (text 410 nm, caption 470 nm, F3b axis 421 nm) and the F5 caption gives 7 W/cm2 where the text gives 1 W/cm2.

changes: n11 (MEC/pathway, freeze-thaw water-expansion) set spine=false: it had no incoming spine edge, so the spine had two roots; it stays as a side claim explaining n12. Spine 20 -> 19.
o3->n13 mm_op register_colocated_views -> measure_feature_metric: the act that yields '0.227 nm fringe spacing' is measuring a metric on the F2h enlargement, not registering two views.

o15 label: day-22 means re-read from the F5f crop (lasers ~1520 not ~1750; BNs-BSA ~2380 is the highest arm, above PBS ~2100); image_note corrected, the 660 nm arm separates from about day 8, not day 12.

panel_checks.note: F2j is the AFM image with a line profile annotated 14 nm between two green arrows and a 0-20 nm height bar; F2c is the 200 nm-scale TEM of bismuthene. Both carry the node's claim, and the audit (14 nm ~ 35 layers, not 'few-layered') stands.

F2m shows the two stacked Bi 4f spectra. In bismuthene (top) the Bi 4f7/2(Bi) component is roughly half the height of Bi 4f7/2(Bi2O3); in bismuthene oxide (bottom) it is a small shoulder. The Bi2O3 doublet is the largest in both, as the node states.
F5f is the six-arm tumour-volume plot to day 22 and shows the claimed ranking; three of the six day-22 values in the node label were off and were re-read from the crop.

review.audit_summary: Three audits, all fair and all of the 'figure qualifies the text' kind: o2 (AFM 14 nm undercuts 'few-layered'), o5/n21 (XPS shows the NaBH4 reduction is only partial, Bi2O3 still dominant), and the notes' record of the DPBF wavelength quoted three ways (text 410 nm, caption 470 nm, F3b axis 421 nm) and the F5 caption's 7 W/cm2 against the text's 1 W/cm2. None is stated as a contradiction of a spine claim, which is right: every affected node keeps image_support=shown and the qualifier sits on a qualifies edge.
